summary: James Sutherland Cotton was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Magdalen College School, Brighton College (~1859–1862), Winchester College (~1862–1867), and Trinity College, Oxford (~1867–1871), and held a post at Queens' College, Cambridge (1871–1874).

James Tod worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts with the East India Company (~1799–1822) and served as Librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1823–1835).

James W. Benson is an Indologist and linguist who taught James McHugh and Susan J. Rosenfield. He held posts as Assistant Professor in Sanskrit at Harvard University (attested 1999–2003) and at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2004).

James W. Heisig works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Cambridge (~1974–1978), he held posts at Nanzan University (~1978), the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (1978; director 1991–2001), and Pompeu Fabra University.
James Whitehill is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who founded the Columbia Zen Center. He served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested 2000).

Linguist James Wilson Bright studied at Lafayette College (~1873–1877) and Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1882). He taught Edwin Whitfield Fay and Franklin Edgerton, holding posts at Cornell University (~1885–1886) and Johns Hopkins University (~1885–1925).

Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thayé was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Thekchok Dorje (~1833–1868) and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1840–1892), and he taught Karma Tashi Chophel and Khakyab Dorje.

Jamie Hubbard works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Komazawa University under Kazuo Okabe and earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He held a professorship at Smith College (attested 2016).

Jampa Losang Panglung worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1969–1979) and served as a wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1978–2004, attested 2005).
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge and Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (attested 1995).
Jampa Samten is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, serving as Director (attested 1991) and Professor (attested 2015).

Jampa Tegchok studied at Sera Monastery and worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1971–1978), Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1993), and Land of Medicine Buddha (~1998–2001).
Jan C. Heesterman was an Indologist who held posts at Leiden University from 1964 to 1990 and as Professor (attested 2014).
Jan Chozen Bays is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Shodo Harada (~1995) and Taizan Maezumi (attested 2011). Around 2002, she became abbess at Great Vow Zen Monastery.
Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna (attested 2013) under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Jan Gonda worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University (PhD 1923–1929) and Leiden University (1929–1931), later holding posts at Utrecht University (1932–1950) and the University of Chicago.

Jan Jaworski was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw (~1922–1928) under Stanisław Schayer, and later studied under Jean Przyluski (~1928–1930).

Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University (~1907–1911). He taught Erik Zürcher and Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé, and held posts at Leiden University in 1919 and from 1930 to 1954.

Jan N. Bremmer is a religious studies and history scholar. He studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (~1962–1970) and the University of Bristol (~1974–1979), and held posts at Utrecht University (~1974–1990) and the University of Groningen (~1990–2009).

Jan Nattier studied at Indiana University and Harvard University, specializing in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. She held professorships at Macalester College, the University of Hawaii, Indiana University, Soka University, and Stanford University.
